data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The total pay is $855, computed as 40 hours at the base rate ($720) plus 7 overtime hours at the 1.5\u00d7 rate ($189).","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the jurisdiction uses a premium-only method where base is paid for all hours and the overtime premium is added on top, the total would be $909 (47 \u00d7 $18 + 7 \u00d7 $9 = $846 + $63), but this is not the standard method described by the problem.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If overtime were calculated at a different multiplier (e.g., 1.25\u00d7), the total would differ, but the problem explicitly states 1.5\u00d7.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If all 47 hours were paid at the base rate with no overtime premium, the total would be $846, contradicting the problem's stated overtime rule.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Standard piecewise overtime calculation: 40 \u00d7 $18 = $720 for regular hours; 7 \u00d7 ($18 \u00d7 1.5) = 7 \u00d7 $27 = $189 for overtime; 720 + 189 = $855.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
